drivingQuestion: What was ben Azzai's difficulty, given that R' Akiva's distinction seems correct?
outcomeNote: Answered by Rava in the next unit

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן עַזַּאי: מַאי שְׁנָא מִן הַיּוֹשֵׁב כּוּ׳. שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְבֶן עַזַּאי?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «ben Azzai said to» Rabbi Akiva: In «what» way is this person who went overseas «different from one who sits» in his house? Rabbi Akiva said to him: The difference is that with regard to one who sits in his house it would have been possible for him to hear of the court’s reversal, but with regard to that person who went overseas, it would not have been possible for him to hear of the court’s reversal. The Gemara asks: «Rabbi Akiva said well to ben Azzai.» How did a scholar of the caliber of ben Azzai fail to understand that distinction?
